key_insight: PDMD improves fast video diffusion distillation by filtering out critic errors that accumulate during training. This prevents the oversaturation and artifact buildup seen in standard DMD, making low-NFE video generation more stable.
problem_solved: The paper addresses instability in Distribution Matching Distillation for video diffusion models, where repeated student updates amplify critic mistakes and gradually degrade sample quality.
method: Identify critic errors as the source of progressive sample degradation in DMD training.
Introduce Projected Distribution Matching Distillation (PDMD) to project or filter the learning signal so harmful critic noise is reduced before it compounds.
Maintain the speed benefits of few-step distillation while improving visual fidelity and training stability for long spatiotemporal video sequences.
impact: For practitioners, PDMD offers a more reliable path to fast video generation with fewer denoising steps. This can reduce compute cost while preserving quality, making diffusion-based video models more practical for real-world deployment.

paper_title: PDMD: Projected Distribution Matching Distillation for Video Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Zimo Wang, Junkun Yuan, Angtian Wang, Haotian Yang, Canyu Zhang
